key_insight: Across the pseudo-boiling line, strong viscosity and density gradients fundamentally reshape vortex evolution, producing vorticity behavior that departs from the classical Oseen solution and can even generate reverse vorticity.
engineering_relevance: For supercritical-fluid systems near critical conditions, vortex mixing, transport, and stability cannot be modeled with constant-property assumptions because thermal stratification can trigger new viscous vorticity mechanisms.
method: Axisymmetric vortex-column simulation in weakly compressible supercritical CO2
Low-Mach multi-dimensional flow solver with imposed radial thermal stratification
Cases spanning hot/cold vortex cores and pressures near the critical pressure
evidence_signal: The paper evaluates vorticity evolution under varying core temperatures and ambient pressures and identifies three viscous mechanisms that become significant across the pseudo-boiling line.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on low-Reynolds-number axisymmetric configurations, so extension to fully 3D, higher-Re flows may require additional validation.
paper_title: Dynamics of a vortex column of supercritical fluid across the pseudo-boiling line
